stem: When explaining posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) epidemiology during evaluation, which organ-involvement pattern aligns with standard references?

options.text: The disease may involve single or multiple organs
PTLD is limited to the transplanted allograft only
Multiorgan involvement never occurs in PTLD
PTLD involves skin only and never visceral sites

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD may involve single or multiple organs and is often extranodal, with involvement of sites such as the gastrointestinal tract, lung, or kidney.

rationale_incorrect.B: PTLD may involve organs beyond the allograft, including extranodal sites.
rationale_incorrect.C: Single or multiple organ involvement is specifically described.
rationale_incorrect.D: Visceral and extranodal involvement such as GI tract, lung, or kidney may occur.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 1. Epidemiology → d.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: May involve single or multiple organs

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 1.d. (may involve single or multiple organs); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Single/multiple-organ involvement angle distinct from extranodal epidemiology in malignancy combo (cctc-3112) and GI-perforation presentation (cctc-2130); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.

stem: A lung transplant recipient develops sore throat and tonsillar enlargement several months post-transplant. Which PTLD presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Tonsillitis may be part of PTLD clinical presentation
Tonsillar symptoms exclude PTLD from the differential
PTLD never involves the upper airway or tonsils
Tonsillitis indicates only bacterial streptococcal infection and never PTLD

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include tonsillitis along with mononucleosis-like symptoms, fever, lymphadenopathy, and upper respiratory infection.

rationale_incorrect.B: Tonsillitis is listed among PTLD presentations rather than excluding it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Upper airway and tonsillar involvement may occur in PTLD.
rationale_incorrect.D: Tonsillitis may be part of PTLD presentation and requires clinical evaluation rather than assuming a single etiology.

stem: When teaching about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) during evaluation, which pulmonary presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: PTLD never produces pulmonary or visceral masses
Pulmonary PTLD is limited to isolated graft tenderness without lesions
Visceral masses occur only in kidney recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include lung lesion or visceral mass along with systemic and gastrointestinal symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Lung lesions and visceral masses are specifically listed presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Pulmonary lesions may occur rather than being limited to graft tenderness alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Lung and visceral involvement is described across solid-organ transplant recipients rather than kidney recipients alone.

stem: A coordinator is updating PTLD recognition teaching for the evaluation team. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: PTLD may involve single or multiple organs.
Tonsillitis may be part of PTLD clinical presentation.
Weight loss is never associated with PTLD.
Lung lesion or visceral mass may occur with PTLD.

explanation.rationale_correct: Single or multiple organ involvement, tonsillitis, and lung or visceral masses are cited PTLD features. Statement III is false because weight loss is listed among clinical presentations.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—lung lesion or visceral mass may occur.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because weight loss is among listed PTLD symptoms.
